title: Private Node Residency Policy Engine and Evidence Stream for Planned Evacuation Windows
creator: Marco Rivera
description:
Goal: Implement a policy engine that enforces per-customer residency constraints for Private/VPC and on-prem nodes, automatically generates verifiable evidence bundles for planned evacuation windows, and exposes safe, auditable regional failover controls that are compatible with customers' legal/regulatory retention settings. This ticket covers design, implementation, and rollout of the orchestration layer and evidence stream used by private deployment agents (on-prem and VPC).

Scope:
- Policy engine to evaluate residency rules (region allow-lists, time-bound evacuation windows, retention/TTL obligations) before authorizing a failover lane.
- Evidence stream generator that aggregates signed metadata (node IDs, region, retention policy, timestamps, KMS-wrapped keys) into exportable audit bundles for compliance teams.
- Safe failover gating: allow scheduled/controlled evacuation (maintenance or policy-triggered) while preventing automatic failover that would violate active residency constraints.
- Console controls + API for customers to declare evacuation windows, retention overlays, and emergency override flows (with mandatory signed approval).
- Integration with routing/orchestration: when policy denies a failover, route requests to local compatible capacity or enforce a hard-deny to callers depending on customer policy.

Non-Goals:
- This ticket does not implement on-prem packaging or the private control-plane UI redesign; those are separate. It does not change token billing or usage metering internals (aside from labeling evidence).

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Policy engine accepts a JSON policy and refuses/permits failovers deterministically; unit tests for >90 policy permutations.
- Evidence bundles generated for each planned evacuation: contain signed node roster, region IDs, retention TTLs, and an audit hash; bundles stored in customer-owned S3 or pushed to customer webhook.
- Failover API responds with a clear reason code when blocked by residency policy and surfaces remediation actions.
- End-to-end test covering planned evacuation window: schedule evacuation, verify policy enforcement, produce evidence bundle, and validate bundle signature with KMS test key.
- Console/API docs and a simple playbook for SOC/Compliance teams describing how to request an emergency override.

Design notes:
- Policy representation: small DSL built on top of Rego-like rules but serialized as normalized JSON to avoid depending on OPA. Policy includes: allowed_regions, prohibited_regions, evacuation_windows (RFC3339 start/end), retention_override (min_retention_days), and emergency_override_allowed(boolean).
- Evaluation path: policy-engine runs inside the private control-plane agent; it queries node state (zone, datacenter, node-id), associated retention profiles, and decides PASS/DEFER/FAIL. PASS allows failover lane, DEFER returns 202 with planned action and schedule, FAIL returns 403-like response with residence_violation code.
- Evidence stream: generator batches events per-evacuation, computes SHA-256 manifest, signs manifest with RP-KMS (customer-managed key if available), stores bundle in encrypted customer S3 (or returns via POST to customer-provided URL). Retention metadata is attached to bundle as cleartext to satisfy auditors while payload artifacts remain encrypted.
- Failover modes: "graceful" (drain with local KV cache persist), "quarantine" (deny external requests to evacuated region but keep nodes online for data extraction), "hard-evacuate" (allowed only with emergency override and recorded audit trail).

Trade-offs and constraints:
- We avoid adding a full policy language to reduce customer onboarding friction; using JSON-DSL reduces expressiveness but simplifies validation and reasoning.
- Evidence bundle size could be large for big fleets; initial implementation will snapshot metadata only (no payload logs) and provide links to per-node telemetry if deeper evidence is required.
- Emergency override must be auditable but also usable; we require signed approvals and a 2-person approval recorded in the evidence bundle.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag behind private-runtime.flags.residency_policy (alpha) and enable for internal private staging.
2) Ship policy engine and evidence generator to control-plane agent v0.12 in staging.
3) Run a pilot with two customers (legal/regional ops) for 4 weeks to validate evidence bundle format and webhook delivery.
4) Add console UI for scheduling evacuations + override flow (PM/design ticket to follow).
5) GA after pilot + security review + compliance signoff.

Observability and SLOs:
- Track policy-eval latency (p50/p95) and error rate. Target p95 < 50ms.
- Evidence bundle generation success rate > 99.5% on scheduled evacuations.
- Create a dashboard: private-residency/policy-evals, private-residency/evidence-bundles, private-residency/blocked-failovers. Link in links[].

Security considerations:
- Evidence signing requires KMS integration; prefer customer-managed keys for on-prem. Fall back to Redwood-managed signing only if customer opts out.
- Store only metadata in Redwood logs; avoid storing customer payloads in evidence bundles unless explicitly permitted.
- Security review required before GA (see security_review_required).

Known risks:
- Mis-specified policies may cause spurious hard-denies; provide strong validation and dry-run mode.
- Large fleets may hit bundle generation timeouts; implement streaming uploads and incremental manifests.

Document links and artifacts: see links field for PRD, draft schema, and dashboard mockups.

2026-03-03: Pilot onboarding with Customer A completed smoke test; evidence bundles received but customer requested CSV-friendly node roster in addition to JSON manifest. Updated producer to include CSV export. - Liang

2026-03-10: E2E smoke: policy-eval p95=34ms in staging; evidence generation success rate 99.6%. Raised follow-ups: (1) retention TTL mapping for legacy retention profiles, (2) dashboard alert tuning. Preparing pilot retro and GA checklist. - Marco
notes: Design feedback: PM suggests adding a dry-run flag so customers can test policy without enforcement. Added to backlog.
SRE: Ensure policy-eval runs locally in agent to avoid control-plane latency during failover decision path.
Compliance: Evidence bundle must persist an immutable timestamp and signer identity; store audit hash in immutable store (work with infra).
